sources.notes: EBA news and press releases: consultations, RTS/ITS, work programme, risk assessments, DORA/MiCA items. Preferred over eba.europa.eu/rss.xml, which is an email-alert digest.

Feed: DG FISMA (financial services) news. Commission financial-services news: legislative proposals, consultations and speeches (crypto rules review, banking-sector package, money market funds). The EU legislative source for DORA, FiDA, PSR and AI Act FS items. Sustainability and pensions items are noise.

Combined ECB feed of press releases, speeches and interviews (e.g. Lagarde 'Where AI risks meet', Schnabel 'Central banks on-chain'). Monetary-policy items are noise. 15 items over about 10 days, so poll frequently.
SSM press releases, Supervisory Board speeches and interviews (supervisory priorities, IT/cyber risk, outsourcing). High signal and low volume.
EIOPA news, including joint ESA warnings (e.g. 'ESAs call for vigilance over external dependencies, cyber threats'), DORA and AI governance in insurance. Climate and pensions items are noise.
ESMA news (MiCA review, supervisory priority on digital innovation, DORA/CTPP items). Items have no pubDate: the date sits only in an HTML <time datetime> inside description, so parse that attribute.

Feed: ESRB policy (warnings, recommendations, opinions). Formal ESRB policy instruments, e.g. the June 2026 Warning on systemic cyber risks from frontier AI and consultation responses. Rare items, very high materiality.
ESRB press releases and speeches (e.g. 'Frontier AI models could strain cyber resilience in the financial system, ESRB warns'). Very low volume, high signal for systemic cyber and AI risk.

Feed: central bankers' speeches, hosted by the BIS for central banks worldwide; an item's sources may name the speaker's own central bank as publication. Aggregated speeches by central bankers worldwide (regulator class per brief). High volume: 50 items cover about 2 weeks, and many come from non-target jurisdictions. Duplicates Fed/ECB/BoE speeches, so dedupe by title. RSS 1.0 (RDF) with dc:date.
Carries the FPC Record (cyber/AI systemic risk), AI Consortium minutes, PRA fines and consultations, and RTGS notices. Noisy (MPC, market notices, Court minutes) but the brief requires it.

Feed: Bank of England prudential-regulation (PRA) publications. PRA consultation papers, policy statements, supervisory statements, Dear CEO letters and the Regulatory Digest. The narrowest feed for PRA operational-resilience, outsourcing/CTP and model-risk policy. Insurance and capital items are noise.

Speeches by BoE, PRA and FPC officials, including digital assets, operational resilience and AI (e.g. Sasha Mills on digital assets, Nathanaël Benjamin). Monetary-policy speeches are noise. 50 items cover about 9 months.

FCA's only feed: category parameters redirect to the same feed. Carries press releases, speeches, statements and news stories (crypto gateway, fraud, Consumer Duty). Consultation papers are announced here but not fed directly. pubDate is non-RFC ('Friday, October 2, 2026 - 11:58') and needs custom parsing.

Feed: FCA publications, all types. Added for the owner decision of 2026-10-03 (new formal rules in RT). Carries policy statements (PS), finalised guidance (FG), consultation papers (CP), guidance consultations (GC), feedback statements, multi-firm reviews and good-and-poor-practice findings (e.g. the money-mule review), and research. Statistics and dashboard pages under /data/ are excluded at fetch (exclude_url_patterns): market and service statistics, not instruments (5 of 20 items on 2026-10-03). fca-news carries press releases and speeches, not these documents; a PS or FG announced in both forms a cluster. Type parameters are ignored (same feed). 20 items cover about 3 to 4 weeks. pubDate is non-RFC ('Friday, October 2, 2026 - 10:31'), as in fca-news.

GOV.UK Atom search feed. HMT policy papers and consultations, e.g. G7 Cyber Expert Group Reconnection Framework annex, Modernising Payment Services Regulation, UK–US Financial Regulatory Working Group statements. Preferred over the HMT news feed (fiscal and political noise). Treasury Minutes and tax consultations are noise.

CFPB press releases, remarks and rules (e.g. joint final rule on uniform financial data standards, complaint-system changes). Relevant to the fraud and data domains (open banking / 1033, data standards). Moderate volume, some consumer-education noise.

Feed: GovDelivery topic USFDIC_19 (Financial Institution Letters). Item links are content.govdelivery.com bulletin wrappers, never citable (FILTER 2.7.2, 7.8): cite the letter's own fdic.gov page, registered with add-manual.mjs --extra (publication 'FDIC', class regulator). Financial Institution Letters, the FDIC's guidance channel to banks (e.g. proposed interagency TPRM guidance, highly sensitive information during exams, GENIUS Act reporting). Disaster-relief FILs are recurring noise.

Feed: GovDelivery topic USFDIC_28 (Speeches & Testimony). Item links are content.govdelivery.com bulletin wrappers, never citable (FILTER 2.7.2, 7.8): cite the fdic.gov page, registered with add-manual.mjs --extra (publication 'FDIC', class regulator). FDIC's official GovDelivery feed for Chairman and Director speeches, testimony and statements (CAMELS reform, resolution, innovation). fdic.gov has no native RSS (all rss.xml paths return 404). It includes some board-meeting notices and quarterly banking profile releases. Low volume.

Feed: Board press releases, Banking & Consumer Regulatory Policy. The narrowest Fed press feed carrying proposals, guidance and interagency statements (e.g. proposed interagency third-party risk management guidance, stress-test transparency). Preferred over press_all, which adds approvals and enforcement noise.

Speeches by Board members, covering supervision, payments, AI and stablecoins (e.g. Waller, 'Payments in the Age of AI Agents'; Bowman on regulatory modernisation). About 15 items over 5 weeks. pubDate is wrapped in CDATA, so strip it before parsing.

Feed: Board 'SR and CA letters, manuals' (Supervision and Regulation and Consumer Affairs letters, supervision manuals). Added for the owner decision of 2026-10-03 (new formal guidance and exam notices in RT). The Fed's channel for supervisory guidance and examination letters (e.g. SR 26-2 revised model risk management guidance, SR 26-3 fraud-related information sharing, SR 26-6 FAQs on verifiable digital credentials under the CIP rule), many of which get no press release in fed-press-bcreg. Headlines are bare letter numbers ('SR 26-6'): the subject is in the lead. Old letters reappear with a new date when revised, superseded or rescinded; a rescission of a technology-risk letter counts as new, a re-dating or restatement does not. 15 items, low volume.

Congressional testimony, mainly the Vice Chair for Supervision's 'Supervision and Regulation' testimony and Monetary Policy Reports. Low volume and high signal on supervisory direction. One item has a malformed date that parses to 1899, so guard date parsing.

Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from the CFPB. Relevant for open-banking and data rules (section 1033, Financial Data Transparency Act data standards) and fraud-related Regulation E changes; threshold adjustments and lending rules are off-domain. Often empty: 0 items in the 30-day window on 2026-10-03, last rule 2026-06-25 (FR API). The rules shared by every fedreg-* source are in the notes of fedreg-occ-final-rules.

Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from the FDIC. Mostly joint banking-agency rules and deposit-insurance rules; the FDIC usually also issues a Financial Institution Letter (fdic-fils). The rules shared by every fedreg-* source are in the notes of fedreg-occ-final-rules.

Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from the Federal Reserve Board. Carries amendments to the Board's Regulations (A, D, LL, YY and others), capital and stress-test rules (off-domain) and joint banking-agency rules. The adoption is usually announced earlier in fed-press-bcreg. The rules shared by every fedreg-* source are in the notes of fedreg-occ-final-rules.

Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from FinCEN. The only FinCEN feed in the registry (fincen-news-releases is a page source). Carries AML/CFT program and reporting rules, special measures and geographic targeting orders. A special measure or order aimed at one named institution is enforcement-like, never an RT instrument. The rules shared by every fedreg-* source are in the notes of fedreg-occ-final-rules.

Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from the NCUA. The only NCUA source in the registry: credit-union rules (e.g. cyber incident notification, third-party servicing). Rules arrive in batches after board meetings, so the feed is often empty: 0 items in the 30-day window on 2026-10-03, last batch 2026-08-06 (FR API). The rules shared by every fedreg-* source are in the notes of fedreg-occ-final-rules.

sources.publication: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.notes: Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from the OCC. Added for the owner decision of 2026-10-03 (new formal rules in RT). Rules shared by every fedreg-* source: (1) type RULE carries final and interim final rules, and also corrections ('; Correction'), effective- or compliance-date delays and extensions, which are not new instruments. (2) The feed always spans the last 30 days; a few items a month per agency. (3) Links are federalregister.gov document pages, the public primary text, and are citable; publication is the issuing agency's common name (FILTER 7.8), never 'Federal Register', the journal that prints it. (4) A joint rule carries the same URL in each issuing agency's fedreg feed (also_in). (5) Federal Register publication often follows the agency's own adoption release by days or weeks; if that release is already in the archive or this run, the Federal Register entry is the same instrument, not new. (6) pubDate is midnight ET of the issue date (sent as 04:00 GMT), hours before the issue goes online, so fetch dates each entry from its URL (/documents/YYYY/MM/DD/) as a calendar date (collect.mjs URL_DATE_RULES) and every run that day collects it. (7) When registering a federalregister.gov page with add-manual.mjs --extra, pass the issuing agency as publication: host matching would otherwise borrow the label of the first fedreg-* source in this file.

Feed: Federal Register API RSS, documents of type RULE from the SEC. The SEC's own RSS page points to the Federal Register for rules. Relevant for Regulation S-P, Regulation SCI, cyber disclosure and market-infrastructure resilience rules; quorum, fee and Form PF compliance-date items are noise. The adoption is usually announced earlier in sec-press-releases. The rules shared by every fedreg-* source are in the notes of fedreg-occ-final-rules.

News Releases listing page. FinCEN has no RSS (every rss.xml/feed path returns 404, and the GovDelivery topic IDs are not public). This listing announces FinCEN alerts, advisories, financial trend analyses and AML rulemaking, which are essential for the fraud domain (e.g. digital-asset scam and deepfake typologies). Entries carry datetime attributes. Node fetch had one intermittent connect timeout; curl was reliable.
Hearings, markups, bills passed and chair statements. Useful for legislative direction on digital assets, AI and data. Moderate partisan framing.

sources.publication: New York State Department of Financial Services
sources.notes: Industry Letters listing page. NYDFS has no RSS (rss.xml returns 404; GovDelivery bulletins.rss returns 406). This page is the canonical channel for Part 500 cyber guidance and AI letters (e.g. 2026-05-21 frontier-AI cyber risk letter, 2026-09-10 cyber risk-assessment guidance). It lists the full archive of about 300 links, with URLs in both /industry_guidance/ and /industry-guidance/ forms; diff on new slugs.

sources.publication: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.notes: Feed: OCC Bulletins. Supervisory guidance bulletins with high signal for tech risk, e.g. 'Cybersecurity Supervision Work Program', 'Third-Party Risk Management: Proposed Guidance', core-provider supervision, and BSA/AML FAQs.

sources.publication: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.notes: OCC news releases, including the Comptroller's remarks and statements (the OCC has no separate speeches feed). Some routine noise (CRA evaluations, trading revenue), but it carries policy and enforcement direction.

Feed: SEC press releases. Added for the owner decision of 2026-10-03 (new formal rules and exam notices in RT): final-rule adoptions are announced here days or weeks before Federal Register publication (fedreg-sec-final-rules), and Division of Examinations notices appear here and not in sec-speeches-statements (e.g. 'SEC's Division of Examinations Announces New Exam Handbook', 2026-10-01; the annual examination priorities). About half the items are individual enforcement cases: facts for EV E2d only, never RT, and the firm is never named. Also carries proposals, exemptive relief and roundtable notices. 25 items cover about 6 weeks. The SEC accepted the declared UA.

Commissioner and staff speeches and statements, including a statement on every major rule proposal (crypto custody, exam handbook, staff statements). Preferred over pressreleases.rss, which is dominated by individual enforcement cases. The SEC accepted the declared UA.

The only working feed: the type parameter is ignored, so majority, minority and hearings return the same content. Low signal-to-noise, dominated by partisan member statements. Kept for hearings and bills; needs a strict materiality filter.

Feed: GovDelivery topic USTREAS_49 (All Treasury Press Releases). No official treasury.gov press-release feed exists (re-checked 2026-10-02): the press-releases page offers only this GovDelivery subscription, /news/press-releases/feed and similar paths time out, and home.treasury.gov/rss.xml is a stale site-wide feed of SSBCI FAQ pages (newest 2026-07-22). Item links are content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USTREAS/bulletins/... mailing-list wrappers, never citable (FILTER 2.7.2, 7.8): cite the release's own page under home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/, registered with add-manual.mjs --extra (publication 'U.S. Department of the Treasury', class regulator). Noisy, with sanctions actions about 70% of items. Kept for FSOC readouts, Treasury AI/cyber/cloud reports, scam-centre and fraud actions, and Secretary testimony. Needs a strict materiality filter.

Publications listing page. ENISA has no working RSS: the legacy /RSS paths and /news/rss return 404, and the rss-feeds page returns 403. Classed as standards_body (EU cyber agency issuing technical guidance and threat landscapes). Examples: ENISA Threat Landscape 2026, NIS2 Technical Implementation Guidance, 'ENISA's view on cybersecurity in the frontier AI era'. 10 entries with datetime attributes.

Feed: BIS and FSI publications. FSI Insights/Briefs/Papers and BIS Bulletins and Papers (e.g. FSI 'When machines attack: frontier AI cyber threats', Bulletin on supervisory screening of LLMs). Mixed: BIS economics working papers are noise, so filter hard.
Speeches by BIS General Manager, FSI and Innovation Hub heads (e.g. 'Supervising banks in an AI-shaped economy'). Low volume, signals direction of international standard-setting.

Feed: media releases, including BCBS, CPMI, CPMI-IOSCO and FSI; for a committee release an item's sources may name the committee (e.g. Basel Committee on Banking Supervision) as publication. The only BIS feed that announces BCBS and CPMI standards and consultations (BIS lists no committee-specific feeds; bcbs.rss and cpmi.rss return 404). Examples: BCBS ICT risk management report, CPMI-IOSCO cyber resilience toolkit for FMIs and third-party discussion paper. Low volume, very high signal.

FSB publications, press releases and meetings (e.g. operational-resilience public-private roundtable, third-party risk, AI monitoring). FSB's per-content-type feeds all return 0 items, so this site-wide feed is the only working one. Low volume.

Media releases listing page. IOSCO's RSS (iosco.org/rss/rss.xml) is stale (last item 2023-05-24) and /rss/news.xml returns 403. This listing works with the declared UA and shows 20 releases per page, each with a date and a PDF link (IOSCONEWSnnn.pdf), e.g. the 2026-09-08 CPMI-IOSCO FMI cyber-resilience toolkit.

Cross-class find, classified standards_body; pass to the standards_body pass for dedupe. Publishes PCI standard releases (Secure Software Lifecycle v2.0, Key Management and Operations v1.0) and AI-systems security guidance. It also carries podcast and sponsor-showcase posts ('The AI Exchange') that are noise.

Feed: NCSC Guidance. Classed as standards_body because it publishes UK national cyber guidance and frameworks (PQC migration timelines, Software Security Code of Practice, ransomware payment guidance, MSP selection). Low volume, about 20 items over 2.5 years. MyNCSC service notes are minor noise. NCSC alerts and news belong to vendor_threat_research (see rejected).

Atom feed of NIST SP, IR and CSWP drafts open for public comment (e.g. IR 8613 multi-cloud security, CSF quick-start guides). The only surviving CSRC feed: the old metafeeds (all.rss, publications.rss, news.rss) all return 404.

Feed: Cybersecurity Insights blog. NIST's official channel announcing and explaining framework work and RFIs (e.g. NVD future and AI-enabled vulnerability management feedback call, agentic-AI identity). Low volume, about 40 items over 2 years. Some sector-specific OT pieces are noise.

Feed: Information Technology news and events. The working NIST topic feed for cyber and AI work (NCCoE drafts, agentic-AI identity concept paper, CSF 2.0 profiles, AI-for-CSF comment calls). The 'cybersecurity' and 'artificial intelligence' topic feeds return 0 items. Some events carry future dates (4 of 40), so ignore future-dated items.

Page source: the EBF site (now ebf.eu, Drupal) exposes no feed (/feed and /rss.xml return 404). The policy-insights listing carries EBF consultation responses and position papers (AMLA, FATF R16 payment transparency, EBA/DDA). It is the EU banking-industry voice on DORA, the AI Act and PSR files. The sibling listing https://ebf.eu/news-insights/news (about 9 entries, mostly press releases) is optional. The www.ebf.eu host rate-limits (429), so use the bare ebf.eu host.

Practitioner body for cyber risk quantification (FAIR/FAIR-CAM). Covers CRQ methods, AI-risk reporting and board-level risk economics. Content is non-profit but vendor-adjacent, as it was founded by RiskLens (now Safe Security), and posts are mostly opinion. It is kept because it is the only feed carrying the risk-quantification domain from a sector body.

Public newsroom: strategy, Critical Providers Program, UK FSCCC stewardship, leadership changes. Some items are press mentions bracketed with the outlet name (e.g. '[Wall Street Journal]'). Low volume, about 10 items a year. Member advisories are not public. Sheltered Harbor is now hosted on fsisac.com and its announcements appear here.

ORX is the Operational Riskdata eXchange. ORX public blog (HubSpot). It includes press releases, the monthly Top 5 ORX News losses, Top Risk Review, Cyber Risk Horizon, major ICT incidents, and CTP/ECB AI-cyber letter analysis. Core source for op-risk data and risk quantification. The news.orx.org loss database is login-only.

Operator of UK retail payment systems (Faster Payments, Bacs, Confirmation of Payee). Posts responses to PSR, BoE and HMT consultations on APP-fraud controls, CoP, RTGS/CHAPS hours and future retail payments infrastructure. Position work covering fraud and resilience.

Page source: UK Finance has no usable feed. Its /rss.xml is an all-content feed (people profiles, events) that crowds out press releases. Essential for UK fraud data (Annual Fraud Report, APP reimbursement), tokenised deposits, and payments trends. Akamai allows the honest ReadinessSignal UA, the only user agent the pipeline sends. Newest entry is dated 24 Sep 2026.

Cybersecurity category only. Covers CISA alerts relevant to banks, sector AI-agent principles, state examiner AI-risk tools, and agency scrutiny of core providers. The main feed is too broad (mortgage, HR, people).

Fraud tag: FCC robocall and spoofing rules, FTC impersonation-scam actions, FinCEN trend analyses, scam legislation. Fraud is a tag on this site; /category/fraud/ returns 404. Overlaps with the cybersecurity feed, so dedupe by URL.

All BPI posts: statements, comment letters, BPInsights. Includes fraud/scams legislation, stablecoin and GENIUS Act letters, and supervisory policy. About 1 post a day, so the full feed is kept. The narrower category/cybersecurity/feed/ works (10 items, newest 2026-09-01) but would miss the fraud and AI items.
Steward of the CRI Profile, the FS adaptation of NIST CSF, and the FS AI risk-management framework. Low volume, with releases of new profile versions, AI resources and sector cyber goals.

Abbreviation: FSSCC. US sector coordinating council: reconnection framework, CISA/NCIRP responses, PQC guidance, cloud steering-group letters. Very low cadence; the last post was 2025-12-16. The feed works and costs little, but drop it if it is still silent at the next review.

Page source: Nacha's /rss.xml only carries Same Day ACH case studies, which are off-topic. The news listing has ACH rule changes (fraud monitoring, funds availability, IAT), Payments Innovation Alliance cybersecurity and stablecoin work, and risk-management guidance. It also includes partner announcements, which are noise. Newest entry is dated 1 Oct 2026.

DW English business section. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): Germany's international public broadcaster. Free to read. Low volume (20 items over about a month): EU markets, banking and corporate stories, occasional cyber and AI-policy items. RSS 1.0 (RDF); links carry a ?maca= tracking parameter. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RDF, 20 items, newest 2026-10-02. No DW technology feed works (rss-en-sci returns an empty body).

Euronews Next (technology) vertical. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): pan-European broadcaster. Free to read. EU AI-policy, cyberattack and data-protection stories (e.g. state-linked crypto heists, AI-agent intrusions, EU cyber-shield audits), mixed with science and gadget items the lexicon drops. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 50 items over about 2 weeks, 12 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02. Chosen over the Euronews business theme feed, which is mostly macro and carries few leads.
EU tech and AI policy (EU AI safety stance, digital sovereignty, Commission tech files). It is the only working EU tech-policy news feed found; Euractiv returns 403.

Main feed, headline and one-line standfirst only. It is the only specialist press for op risk, model risk and risk quantification (scenario frameworks, resolution, CRO moves). It is noisy because most items are markets and derivatives, so the materiality filter must work hard. The category feeds are worse: operational-risk is stale since 2025-05 and sponsored, and risk-management has no leads. Responses are gzip-compressed.

BBC News business section. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): UK national broadcaster. Broad (economy, energy, retail), so prefilter strict; carries UK bank outages, retail cyberattacks and fraud stories. Paywall: free in the UK and most regions, but bbc.com has shown a dynamic paywall to US visitors since June 2025 and the routine may run from a US address, so treated as headline-and-lead only (set paywalled false only if the routine is confirmed to run outside the US). The www.bbc.co.uk URL redirects to feeds.bbci.co.uk; it is registered on www.bbc.co.uk so article URLs (www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/...) match this source for add-manual.mjs --extra. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200 after redirect, RSS, 55 items, 38 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02.

BBC News technology section. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): UK national broadcaster. AI, cyber, data and platform stories. Paywall and URL notes as bbc-news-business (dynamic paywall for US visitors; the www.bbc.co.uk URL redirects to feeds.bbci.co.uk). Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200 after redirect, RSS, 21 items over about 4 weeks, 13 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02.
Financial-crime channel: fraud, scams, sanctions evasion, bank cyberattacks. Same future-dated webinar caveat as the security channel. Overlaps with the security channel, so dedupe by URL.

Security channel: FS breaches (Revolut, Bitget), scams policy, PQC. The feed embeds future-dated sponsored webinar items (5 seen), so drop any item with pubDate in the future. Unknown channel names (risk, regulation) silently return the all-headlines feed.

FT cyber-security topic feed, headline and standfirst only. Major exchange hacks, AI-enabled cybercrime, UK security warnings. The narrowest FT feed with this signal; the FT banks and fintech topic feeds work but are noisier.

The Guardian business section, UK edition. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): UK national newspaper. Free to read (reader-funded, no paywall). Broad (economy, markets, retail, energy), so prefilter strict; carries UK bank IT failures, retail and supplier cyberattacks, and fraud and scam coverage. Use the /uk/ edition path: /business/rss redirects to an edition chosen by location. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 40 items over about 3 days, newest 2026-10-02.

The Guardian technology section, UK edition. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): UK national newspaper. Free to read. AI, cyber, data protection and platform regulation. Narrower tag feeds also work (technology/hacking/rss, technology/data-computer-security/rss, about 20 items a month) if this one proves too noisy. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 32 items, 17 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02.

Security-tagged headlines only. The URL redirects to an api.theregister.com RSS remapper, so follow redirects. Gives UK/EU angle on zero-days, AI-agent incidents and UK security-service warnings. Chosen over the all-headlines feed.
AI section feed: AI agents in banking, Fed data tools, AI security for real-time payments. Some sponsored 'partner insights' items appear, which the filter should drop. Headline and lead only.

Cyber-security section feed (data-security.rss is identical). Bank-specific incidents (core-provider outages, bank offline after cyber incident), NYDFS and Fed supervisory remarks, fraud litigation. Headline and lead only. This is the narrowest AB feed and is used in place of the general feed?rss=true.

Axios main feed (all national topics). General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): US national news outlet. Free to read. Very broad (politics, business, tech, AI and cyber policy), so prefilter strict. Axios Pro items are paywalled and Axios Local items are local press, so both are excluded by URL. Large response (about 1 MB, 100 items over about a week). No per-topic feeds (/feed/technology returns 404). Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 100 items, 53 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02.

Disabled 2026-10-04: the site answers the honest ReadinessSignal user agent with HTTP 403, and the pipeline never impersonates a browser. Published by ISMG (Information Security Media Group). Articles-only ISMG feed: breach roundups, crypto-hack roundups, AI-security and regulatory stories. Items carry no pubDate. The newest date is from the channel pubDate and the top story, so use first-seen time. The feed is network-wide: the GovInfoSecurity articles feed is identical, so do not add it too. Chosen over the /rss-feeds main feed, which mixes in webinars and stale FDIC/FFIEC items. The old feedburner URLs are dead.
US bank regulation, supervisory actions, fintech/bank partnerships, core-provider stories. Mostly business news; the third-party and resilience stories are the target.

All-news feed of about 15 items covering roughly 2 days. Primary reporting on exploited zero-days, ransomware takedowns and breach disclosures. It is often first on incidents affecting FS vendors (Fortinet, Citrix, Cisco). Some items are sponsored 'how-to' pieces, which the materiality filter should drop.

CNBC Finance section. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): US business news broadcaster. Free to read, except CNBC Pro subscriber articles: a page showing a subscription prompt is headline-and-lead only (NP1, NP2). Wall Street, banks, payments and fintech, so prefilter strict; carries bank AI adoption, outage and fraud stories. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 30 items, 11 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02.

CNBC Tech section. General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): US business news broadcaster. Free to read, except CNBC Pro subscriber articles (NP1, NP2). Big-tech, AI, cyber and outage business coverage; market-move items are noise. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 30 items over about 2 days, newest 2026-10-02.
Washington cyber-policy reporting: national cyber director, CISA, sector ISACs, law-enforcement takedowns, exploited zero-days.
Enterprise-risk-oriented cyber news. Covers mass exploitation events, GAO and regulatory-harmonisation stories, and SOC/AI workforce coverage. Good signal-to-noise.
50 items over about 2 weeks. Mixes news (ransomware, nation-state, AI policy) with contributed opinion columns, so expect the filter to drop the columns.

Published by Inside Washington Publishers. Subscription publication covering US federal cyber regulation in detail: CISA incident-reporting final rule, the NCD, sector frameworks, GAO. Its public RSS carries long body text (median about 660 words). Ingest headline plus first paragraph only (lead_words set to 50 as the truncation target) and never fetch articles. One sticky 2024 item sits at the top of the feed.
Investigative reporting on cybercrime, card and identity fraud ecosystems, and data brokers. Publishes 1–2 posts a week with high signal for the fraud and cyber domains.

NYT Technology section, headline and lead only (metered paywall). General or business press for E3 (FILTER 2.7.4): US national newspaper. AI, platform, cyber and crypto stories; some items are cross-filed from Business. Verified 2026-10-02 with the project UA: HTTP 200, RSS, 29 items over about a week, 20 in the last 72 h, newest 2026-10-02. NYT Business (nyt/Business.xml) also works but is high volume (50 items in 2 days).
Payments rails (FedNow, stablecoins), card networks, payments fraud and agentic-commerce risk. Free primary reporting.
US tech and AI policy: White House AI accords, state frontier-AI laws, congressional AI moves. Carries the AI-governance signal for US firms. It is mostly political, so expect a low FS hit rate.
Latest 10 items. Covers vulnerabilities under active exploitation, threat-actor campaigns and AI-agent attack reporting. Weekly 'In Other News' roundups are low value.
Security category only. Strong original breach reporting, including fintech and consumer-data breaches, plus urgent-patch stories. Some startup-funding items are noise.

The Record from Recorded Future News. Editorially independent newsroom with strong cyber-policy, nation-state and ransomware reporting. The feed returns only the latest 5 items, but a fetch 4 times a day is enough.

Technology section, headline and standfirst only. This is the current Dow Jones feed host; the old feeds.a.dj.com URLs have been frozen since 2025-01-27. Mostly AI and big-tech business, with occasional major cyber or AI-risk scoops. No public Risk & Compliance Journal or WSJ Pro Cyber feed exists.

Feed: Security Advisories. Numbered advisories, issued only for critical or exploited vulnerabilities (Citrix, F5, SAP, SharePoint), with recommended actions. Very high signal for the EU. pubDate uses named zones (CEST/CET), so the parser must map these to offsets.

ESET Research, published on WeLiveSecurity. No research-only feed exists, so this is the main WeLiveSecurity feed. Keep only items whose <category> is 'ESET research' (23 of 100). Those items cover APT reports, UEFI/Secure Boot flaws and the threat report. Drop consumer-awareness posts. Newest research item: 2026-09-17.

Mobile banking-malware and device-takeover fraud research (StreamRat, Manic), directly on point for bank fraud. Mixed with some vendor and fireside posts, so keep only malware-analysis items. Low volume.
Original vulnerability and threat research, including AI-platform data-leak research. The weekly 'Threat Intelligence Report' digests are secondary and can be dropped.
Securelist blog. Kaspersky GReAT research on APTs, ransomware and banking and fintech-targeting malware. Technical, low volume.
Pre-auth exploit analysis of edge appliances (Citrix NetScaler, F5 BIG-IP, ColdFusion), often published within days of disclosure. Gives an early read on how exploitable perimeter kit is.

Feed: NCSC News. NCSC alerts and joint attributions, for example the Citrix NetScaler exploitation alert and Iranian and Russian actor exposures. Some institutional announcements are mixed in. This is the UK technical-alert channel, since NCSC no longer runs a separate advisories feed.
Threat-research category only: active-exploitation notes, loaders and ransomware tradecraft, Patch Tuesday analysis. The old news.sophos.com URL redirects here.

AWS Post-Event Summaries listing page. No feed. Listing page of AWS's formal post-event summaries, published only for major multi-customer disruptions (for example the October 2025 DynamoDB US-EAST-1 outage). Rarely changes, so cheap to diff. Essential cloud concentration-risk post-mortems.

Azure status history page (Post Incident Reviews). No feed: the status RSS carries live incidents only. Server-rendered history page of preliminary and final PIRs with Tracking IDs and root-cause sections. Essential for cloud concentration risk.

CERT Coordination Center, Carnegie Mellon SEI; Vulnerability Notes feed. Coordinated vulnerability disclosures (VU#), for example auth-library signature bypasses and firmware SMM flaws. Moderate volume. Useful for multi-vendor and supply-chain disclosures that vendors may not publicise.

Feed: CISA Alerts. CISA alerts on actively exploited zero-days and emergency guidance, for example the Citrix NetScaler zero-days. Most items are 'CISA Adds N KEV' notices that duplicate cisa-kev, so dedupe on CVE ID.

Feed: CISA Malware Analysis Reports. Deep technical malware analysis reports (BRICKSTORM, FIRESTARTER, Ivanti and SharePoint exploitation). Only a few per year, so cheap to poll, and every item is technical.

Feed: CISA Cybersecurity Advisories (joint CSAs). Narrowest CISA feed: joint Five Eyes/FBI/NSA technical advisories (#StopRansomware, state-actor TTPs, AI distillation campaigns) with IOCs and mitigations. Low volume, very high signal.

CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (JSON). Authoritative JSON list of CVEs confirmed exploited in the wild (catalogVersion 2026.10.01). The main trigger for patch-now items in the cyber and third-party domains. Diff on dateAdded each run.

Talos Intelligence blog. Talos threat spotlights, actor and malware research, and vulnerability discoveries. Items carry <category>. Drop 'Threat Source newsletter' and detection-rule update posts. No working tag feed was found.

Cloudflare blog, post-mortem tag. Detailed root-cause post-mortems of Cloudflare outages and route leaks, plus the 'Code Orange' resilience programme. A key concentration-risk provider for financial services. A few items a year.

GitHub blog, Availability Reports tag. Monthly incident summaries with root cause and remediation for GitHub, a critical third party for financial-services software delivery. Resilience and third-party domains. One item a month.
Open-source supply-chain vulnerability research and Advisory Database insight. Relevant to the third-party and software supply-chain domain. A few maintainer how-to posts. Low volume.
Deep exploit and vulnerability research (0-click chains, Windows exploitation techniques). The project moved from blogspot, which now redirects here. Low volume.

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), including Mandiant. GTIG/Mandiant research on exploitation campaigns, financially motivated actors (ShinyHunters, BREEZE COMET), AI threat tracking and incident-response findings. This is Google's own feed host. The cloud.google.com/blog path returns HTML; a feedburner mirror also exists.

Threat-intelligence topic feed rather than the whole Security blog. Covers actor tradecraft (Storm-/Blizzard naming), exploited CVE tracking and cloud identity attacks. High relevance for Microsoft-heavy financial-services estates.
Threat briefs on exploited zero-days, cloud and Kubernetes attack research, and incident-response learnings. A few consulting-promo posts get through, but it is mainly technical.

Proofpoint Threat Insight blog. Threat-research-only feed: email-borne campaigns, fraud actors and state-aligned phishing (TA-numbered actors). Strong for the fraud and social-engineering domain. The corporate rss.xml is excluded as marketing.

Rapid7 Emergent Threat Response (ETR) tag. ETR tag feed only: rapid technical write-ups of exploited-in-the-wild CVEs (Cisco SD-WAN, Citrix). Used instead of the full Rapid7 blog, which is marketing-heavy.
SentinelOne's research unit. Technical research on DPRK TraderTraitor (a crypto and finance-targeting actor), agentic-AI intrusions and state threat landscapes. Research-only labs feed.
Incident-response-led discoveries of zero-day exploitation (Chrome/Windows chains, SonicWall, BRICKSTORM). Low volume, high signal. /blog/feed/ redirects to HTML; use /feed/.

Feed: ECB Working Paper Series. ECB staff research, for example 'Artificial intelligence and financial markets'. High volume (about 15 in 2.5 weeks), mostly monetary. Narrower than the all-publications feed (rss/pub.html).

Feed: ESRB publications. ESRB reports, working papers and risk dashboards, including systemic-cyber and AI work such as 'Addressing frontier AI models with cyber capabilities from a financial stability perspective'. Low volume. A macroprudential body, so it may overlap the regulator class.

Listing: cs.CR (Cryptography and Security). Daily academic preprints in security, including LLM and agent security, malware and privacy. High volume (about 100+ a day) and not peer-reviewed, so it needs strict filtering. Included as the leading indicator of new attack classes.
Listing: q-fin.RM (Risk Management). Daily preprints on quantitative risk management: model risk, insurance and AI under Solvency II. Feeds the risk-quantification domain. A handful a day.
Feed: BIS Working Papers. Bank for International Settlements research with original data. Includes stablecoin and DeFi measurement and work on AI and tokenisation, alongside macro papers. RDF format.

Feed: Bank Insights. Bank of England analytical pieces with data, for example 'Frontier AI and the question of governance' and digital banking. Narrower than the full publications feed, which is mostly statistical releases. About 3 a month.

Cross-class find, classified research_analysis rather than industry_trade. Independent UK body that categorises systemic cyber events on a 1–5 scale with £ loss estimates (JLR, retail ransomware, Canvas), using a published methodology. Rare but high-signal for risk quantification. Low cadence; last post 2026-07-08.

Feed: Atlantic Council cybersecurity issue. Fallback for the Cyber Statecraft Initiative, whose program feed is empty. Carries CSI research reports alongside commentary from other programs (about 4 a month). Keep reports with data or method; drop op-eds.

sources.publication: Center for Security and Emerging Technology
sources.notes: CSET, Georgetown University. Center for Security and Emerging Technology research: data-driven AI, compute and talent analysis. Publications-only feed; the main feed mixes in press mentions.

Independent data-science research on cyber-loss frequency and severity, incident notification times and forecast backtesting. The closest public match to the risk-quantification domain. Low volume, with some office-hours posts.
Feed: FEDS Notes (Board staff). Short staff analyses with data, for example AI adoption evidence. Occasionally covers payments, cyber and fintech. Macro-heavy, so low-to-moderate yield.

Feed: Finance and Economics Discussion Series (FEDS). Fed Board staff working papers with original data. Macro-heavy, but includes financial-vulnerability measurement and banking papers. Low yield; relies on the downstream materiality filter.
U.S. Office of Financial Research. Treasury OFR working papers, briefs and blog posts on financial-system data, monitoring and forecasting methods. Original data and transparent methods. Low volume.
